risks.title: Principal Acceleration Upon Default
risks.original_clause:
Section 3. Default and Acceleration
If Borrower fails to make any payment when due, and such failure continues for ten (10) days, Lender may declare the entire unpaid principal balance immediately due and payable.
risks.explanation: A single missed payment or technical default allows the lender to demand immediate lump-sum repayment of the full loan balance.
risks.why_it_matters: Temporary cash flow interruptions could trigger immediate full balance payoff demands and financial distress.
risks.possible_consequences: Immediate demand for full payoff, potential foreclosure, or legal collection proceedings.
suggested_questions: Can a 15-day written notice and grace period be required before acceleration can be declared?
Can acceleration be restricted only to material payment defaults exceeding 60 days?
